THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Though these appeals are listed for admission, with the consent of both counsel, it is taken up for final disposal.
2. Since these two appeals are arising out of same judgment and award, they are clubbed together and decided by common order.

3. While MFA No.202050/2018 is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement, MFA No.200303/2019 is filed by the insurance company challenging the fastening the liability on it and also 9% interest granted on the compensation.
4. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
5. It is the case of the petitioner that on 30.04.2014 at 9:00 p.m. he was proceeding on motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-28/EB-0352 (for short 'motorcycle') towards Kannal village.

Near Domanal Tanda, car bearing registration No.KA-24/5086 ('the offending vehicle' for short), came from the opposite side, in a high speed, in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
In the said accident, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries resulting in permanent partial disability.
Inspite of prolonged treatment, petitioner is not completely cured.
As the owner and insurer, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

6. Respondent No.1 has remained ex parte.
7.

Respondent No.2 filed written statement disputing that accident occurred due to rash or negligent driving of offending vehicle, the age, occupation, income of the petitioner, nature of the injuries sustained by him and that they have resulted in permanent partial disability and also medical expenses incurred for the treatment.
8. Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.

11. Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition filed by the petitioner granting compensation in a sum of Rs.4,64,520/- with interest at 9% per annum and directed respondent No.2 to pay the same as detailed below:

12.
During the course of arguments, learned counsel representing the petitioner submitted that the Tribunal has erred in not considering income of the petitioner at Rs.8,000/- per month.
Having regard to the nature of the injuries sustained, the disability considered by the Tribunal at 12% is on the lower side.
No compensation is granted under the head future medical expenses.
The compensation granted under all other heads is on the lower side and prays to allow the appeal.

13. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 submitted that since the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid driving licence for transport vehicle, the Tribunal has erred in fastening the liability on respondent No.2.
The interest granted at 9% is on the higher side and prays to allow the appeal filed by it and dismiss the appeal filed by the petitioner.
14. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for respondent No.2 and perused the records.

sentences.text: As on the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 20 years, which fact is reflected in the wound certificate.
Therefore, multiplier 18 taken by the Tribunal is correct.
In the absence of proof of exact income, the Tribunal has taken his notional income at Rs.6,000/- p.m.

Since the accident is of the year 2014, based on minimum wages, the notional income ought to have been taken at Rs.7,500/-
p.m.
16.
The Tribunal has considered the disability at 12%.
Having regard to the nature of the injuries suffered, period of treatment, it would be appropriate to take the disability at 15%.

With the income at Rs.7,500/-, multiplier 18 and disability at 15%, the loss of income due to disability is at Rs.7,500/-
x 12 x 18 x 15% = 2,43,000/- as against Rs.1,55,520/- granted by the Tribunal.
17. Based on medical bills, compensation granted in a sum of Rs.2,50,000/- under the head medical expenses is correct.
At the rate of Rs.7,500/-, for a period of three months, the petitioner is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.22,500/- under the head loss of income during laid up period.

18. Having regard to the nature of the injuries suffered which have resulted in permanent partial disability, the compensation granted in a sum of Rs.25,000/- each under the head pain & suffering,
loss of amenities, Rs.3,000/- under the head attendant, diet, conveyance & other charges is on the lower side.
The same is enhanced to Rs.40,000/- each under the head pain & suffering and loss of amenities and Rs.15,000/- under the head attendant, diet conveyance & other charges.
19. The Tribunal has not granted any compensation under the head future medical expenses.
Looking to the nature of injuries sustained, which has resulted in permanent partial disability, I hold that the petitioner is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.25,000/- under this head.

20. Thus, in all the petitioner is entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.6,35,500/-, as against Rs.4,64,520/- granted by the Tribunal as detailed below:

Now coming to the appeal filed by respondent No.2.
Undisputedly the offending vehicle is a commercial vehicle, whereas its driver was holding driving licence to drive a light motor vehicle non-transport.
However, in view of judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited and Others1, he is entitled to drive a light motor vehicle transport also.

sentences.text:
Therefore, the Tribunal is justified in fastening the liability on respondent No.2.
22.
So far as the ground regarding the rate of interest, as held in MFA No.103557/2016 dated 20.03.2018, the Tribunal is not justified in imposing interest more than 6%.
Accordingly, it is reduced to 6%.

23. In the result, both appeals deserves to be allowed in part and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
(2016) 4 SCC 298 - 11 - ORDER
(i) Both the Appeals are allowed in part.

(ii) The appellant is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.6,35,500/- as against Rs.4,64,520/-
granted by the Tribunal together with interest at 6% p.a. (except on Rs.25,000/- granted under the head future medical expenses).

(iii) Respondent No.2/Insurance company shall deposit the compensation amount within a period of six weeks from the date of this order together with interest at 6% p.a. (minus the compensation already paid/deposited).
(iv) Registry is directed to transmit the amount in deposit (if any) along with copy of this order to the Tribunal.
